auth.description: Atlassian API token; the user half is the account email that minted it. This is the same token a Jira connection uses, but it is stored at a separate address and must be supplied again
auth.name: confluence.api_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: The part of your Confluence URL before `.atlassian.net` — if you sign in at `acme.atlassian.net/wiki`, this is `acme`. It is the same site name as your Jira connection, if you have one
config.label: Atlassian site name
config.name: site

config.help: The email of the account that minted the API token. It travels as the username half of the request
config.label: Atlassian account email
config.name: email

config.help: Create one at id.atlassian.com under Security → API tokens. Atlassian shows it once. This is the same kind of token a Jira connection uses — and if you already made one for Jira, that token works here too, but it has to be pasted again: the two connections store it separately
config.label: API token
config.name: api_token

description: Confluence Cloud wiki: find spaces, list the pages in one, read a page's metadata, publish a new page, and comment on one. Page and comment *content* cannot be read back — see the connector's notes

operations.description: List the spaces on the Confluence site, with the id, key and name of each. Takes no argument, and is this connector's `verify`: a bounded read that runs unattended and needs nothing configured beyond the credential. Returns only Confluence's first page of 25 spaces — paging needs the `cursor` and `limit` query parameters this connector cannot send, so a site with more spaces is truncated with no further signal than a `_links.next` this connector cannot follow

_links.description: Pagination envelope. `next` holds the RELATIVE URL of the following page with an opaque cursor embedded in it (`/wiki/api/v2/spaces?limit=25&cursor=…`). **This connector cannot follow it** — the cursor is a query parameter it cannot send (C-30), and the value is a URL rather than the bare token a cursor quirk would need. Its presence means only that more spaces exist

base.description: The Confluence site's base URL, for resolving the relative links above

next.description: Unusable here; see this field's own description. Absent when there is no further page

results.description: This page's spaces — at most 25, and there is no way to fetch the rest

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the space's path in the Confluence UI — append it to the site URL to give a human a link

authorId.description: Account id of whoever created the space. An `accountId`, never a username or email

description.description: EMPTY IN THIS RESPONSE. Populating it needs the `description-format` query parameter, which this connector cannot send

homepageId.description: The space's home page, as a page id — pass it to `confluence-page-get`. This is the usual entry point into a space's content

icon.description: The space's icon, when it has one and `include-icon` was requested — which this connector cannot do, so absent

id.description: The space's id, as a string. This is what `confluence-space-get` and `confluence-space-pages` address it by — **not** the `key`

key.description: The space key, e.g. `ENG`. The short code that appears in a Confluence URL. Human-facing and stable, but the v2 API addresses spaces by `id`

type.description: `global` for an ordinary space or `personal` for a user's own space

operations.description: Get one space by its id, with its key, name, status and home page id. Addressed by the numeric space `id` from `confluence-space-list`, not by the space key that appears in a Confluence URL

params.description: The space's id, from `confluence-space-list`'s `id`. This is the numeric id as a string, not the space key (`ENG`) — the v2 API does not accept a key here
params.name: id

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the space's path in the Confluence UI, and `base`, the site URL to resolve it against

authorId.description: Account id of the space's creator

description.description: EMPTY IN THIS RESPONSE, for the same reason as in `confluence-space-list`: it needs the `description-format` query parameter

homepageId.description: The space's home page, as a page id — the usual entry point into its content

id.description: The space's id, as a string

key.description: The space key, e.g. `ENG` — the short code in a Confluence URL

spaceOwnerId.description: Account id of the space's current owner, or null when it has none

status.description: `current` or `archived`. An archived space still reads

operations.description: List the pages in one space, with the id, title, parent and version of each — the way to discover what a space contains and to resolve a page title to the id the other operations take. **Page bodies are not returned**: the content of each page is empty here, because selecting a body format needs a query parameter this connector cannot send. Returns only Confluence's first page of 25 results; a larger space is truncated

params.description: The space's id, from `confluence-space-list`'s `id` — not the space key
params.name: id

_links.description: Pagination envelope; `next` is a relative URL with an opaque cursor embedded, which this connector cannot follow. See `confluence-space-list`'s own `_links` for the full reason

next.description: Unusable here; its presence means only that the space has more pages

results.description: This page's pages — at most 25 of the space's pages, with no way to fetch the rest

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the page's path in the Confluence UI — the link to give a human, resolved against the site URL

authorId.description: Account id of whoever created the page

body.description: **EMPTY (`{}`) IN THIS RESPONSE.** Confluence populates it only when a `body-format` query parameter selects a representation, and this connector sends none (C-30). Do not report a page as empty on the strength of this field — it says nothing about whether the page has content

id.description: The page's id, as a string — what `confluence-page-get` and `confluence-comment-add` address it by

ownerId.description: Account id of the page's current owner

parentId.description: The page this one sits under in the space's tree, or null for a top-level page. This is how the page hierarchy is reconstructed

parentType.description: What the parent is, e.g. `page` — a page can hang off a whiteboard or database, not only another page

position.description: The page's sort position among its siblings, or null

spaceId.description: The space this page belongs to — the id that was passed in

title.description: The page's title. This is the only content-bearing field this operation returns, and it is what a title-to-id lookup matches on

version.description: The page's current version: `{number, createdAt, message, minorEdit, authorId}`. `number` is the version an update would have to increment — this connector declares no update (see its notes), so it is informational here

authorId.description: Who made the most recent edit

message.description: The edit comment, when the editor left one

operations.description: Read one page's metadata by id — title, space, parent, author, creation time, current version number and the link to open it in Confluence. **The page body is not returned**: selecting a content format needs a query parameter this connector cannot send, so the `body` field comes back empty regardless of whether the page has content. Use this to resolve a page id to its title and URL, not to read what the page says

params.description: The page's id, from `confluence-space-pages`, from a space's `homepageId`, or from `confluence-page-create`'s response
params.name: id

_links.description: `webui` is the page's path in the Confluence UI and `base` is the site URL — join them to give a human a link. `editui` and `tinyui` are the edit and short forms

base.description: The site's base URL, to resolve the paths above against

authorId.description: Account id of whoever created the page. An `accountId`, never a username — it identifies a named person, so read it for what the calling flow needs and do not persist it beyond that

body.description: **EMPTY (`{}`).** Confluence populates this only when a `body-format` query parameter selects a representation (`storage`, `view`, `atlas_doc_format`…), and this connector sends none (C-30). An empty `body` here is a limitation of this connector and says nothing about the page — do not report the page as blank on the strength of it

id.description: The page's id, as a string

lastOwnerId.description: Account id of the previous owner, or null

ownerId.description: Account id of the page's current owner

parentId.description: The page this one sits under, or null for a top-level page

position.description: Sort position among siblings, or null

spaceId.description: The space the page belongs to — pass it to `confluence-space-get` for the space's name and key

status.description: `current` for a live page, or `archived`/`draft`/`trashed`. A trashed page still reads here

title.description: The page's title — the only content-bearing field this operation returns

version.description: The page's current version — returned without asking, because the vendor's `include-version` defaults to true. `number` is what an update would have to increment; this connector declares no update, and its notes say why

authorId.description: Who made the most recent edit

createdAt.description: When this version was created — i.e. when the page was last edited

message.description: The edit comment, when the editor left one

minorEdit.description: Whether the editor marked it a minor edit, suppressing notifications

operations.description:
Publish a new page in a space. The page is created live and visible to everyone who can see the space, is indexed for search, and notifies the space's watchers. It is created at the top level of the space unless the space's own structure places it otherwise, with no labels and no restrictions. Returns the new page's id, title and links. The content is sent as Confluence storage format — XHTML-like markup, e.g. `

text

` — not Markdown and not wiki markup

params.description: Id of the space to publish into, from `confluence-space-list`. The only field Confluence's schema strictly requires
params.name: space_id

params.description: The page's title, as it will appear in the space and in search. Confluence requires titles to be unique within a space and rejects a duplicate with a `400`
params.name: title

params.description:
The page content, in **Confluence storage format**: XHTML-like markup such as `

A paragraph.

A heading

  • An item
`. Plain text is accepted and renders as a single unformatted run. Markdown is **not** converted — it would be stored and displayed literally, asterisks and all
params.name: body

_links.description: `webui` is the new page's path in the Confluence UI and `base` is the site URL; join them to give a human the link to what was just published

authorId.description: The account the token belongs to — a published page is attributed to it, and that name is what other people in the space will see

body.description: Echoes the storage-format content that was sent, under `storage`. This is the one response in this connector that carries a page body — because it is the body the caller supplied, not one Confluence was asked to render

id.description: The new page's id — the only handle on it, and what `confluence-comment-add` and `confluence-page-get` address it by afterwards

parentId.description: The page it was placed under, which Confluence resolves to the space's home page when none was requested

spaceId.description: The space the page was published into

status.description: `current` on a page this operation created

title.description: Echoes the title that was sent

version.description: `{number, createdAt, authorId, minorEdit, message}`, with `number` = 1 on a page just created

operations.description:
Add a footer comment to a page — the comment thread at the bottom, not an inline annotation on selected text. The comment is visible to everyone who can see the page and notifies its watchers; it cannot be restricted to a subset of them. The content is sent as Confluence storage format (`

text

`), not Markdown. Note the page is named in the body rather than in the path, and that this connector cannot read a page's existing comments back

params.description: Id of the page to comment on, from `confluence-space-pages` or `confluence-page-create`. This creates a top-level footer comment on that page; replying to an existing comment is not supported by this operation
params.name: page_id

params.description:
The comment text, in **Confluence storage format**: XHTML-like markup such as `

A comment.

`. Plain text is accepted and renders unformatted. Markdown is **not** converted and would be displayed literally
params.name: body

_links.description: Carries `webui`, the comment's anchored path in the Confluence UI — it opens the page scrolled to this comment — and `base`, the site URL to resolve it against

body.description: Echoes the storage-format content that was sent, under `storage`

id.description: The new comment's id, as a string

pageId.description: The page the comment was attached to — echoes what was sent, and worth checking, since the parent is chosen by which body field was present rather than by the path

parentCommentId.description: Null on a top-level comment, which is all this operation creates

title.description: Confluence's own generated title for the comment, e.g. `Re: <page title>`. Not something the caller sets

version.description: `{number, createdAt, authorId, minorEdit, message}`, with `number` = 1 on a comment just created
